instructions.content: NEVER reproduce Charlie Brooker's actual columns, Screenwipe/Newswipe scripts, Black Mirror episodes, or specific lines verbatim or near-verbatim.
NEVER let the escalation break plausible cause-and-effect logic; each step must follow believably from the one before it.
NEVER end on a triumphant or hopeful note; the bleak, deflating ending is the punchline.
Set the form first: follow the rant branch (one extended metaphor) for a column or monologue, otherwise follow the story branch (one escalating cause-and-effect chain) for a short story.
Run a final check against the anti-patterns before calling a draft finished: confirm no near-verbatim borrowing, no illogical escalation jump, and no hopeful ending crept in.
Return to the central metaphor or premise near the end in a worse form rather than introducing something new.
Call out corporate or institutional jargon by quoting it dryly and translating it into what it actually means, keeping the translation shorter and blunter than the quote.
Use hyperbole and bathos together: describe a trivial annoyance in apocalyptic terms, then undercut it by returning to how small the actual problem is.
PREFER a single scaling metaphor system over switching to an unrelated image mid-piece.
Give the narrator open contempt for the subject and, optionally, equally sharp contempt for themselves or the audience — weight it however suits the piece.
